plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Gain magnitude and lag/settling time at a safe mid power; distinguishes fast-small-gain vs slow-large-gain and gives first steady-state estimate for target 0.5.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.05 toward 0.3-0.5 with decreasing slope, staying below 0.6 and showing non-zero end slope if not yet settled.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Settling time and steady-state gain at u=0.5: E1 still rising at 0.0015/s after 180s, so extending the same hold measures equilibrium without re-warming and tests whether u=0.5 holds target 0.5.
experiments.expected_observation: y rises from ~0.395 toward ~0.45-0.52 with gradually decreasing slope (~0.001/s by end), staying below 0.6; persistent non-zero end slope confirms long time constant and lets us extrapolate steady-state for u=0.5.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether output decays on its own at u=0 and cooling time constant, which determines open-loop stability and whether overshoot can be corrected passively for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If heater with passive loss hypothesis is right, y decays monotonically from ~0.49 toward ~0.1-0.2 with decreasing (less negative) slope, initial slope around -0.001 to -0.002/s, end slope still negative showing not yet fully settled, staying well above 0.05 and never rising.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Linearity of steady-state gain and steady-state input for target: a second amplitude (u=0.6) from current low y discriminates linear vs saturating gain and refines feedforward for y=0.5.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order heater with tau ~120-150s and ambient ~0.05 is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.19 toward ~0.58 inf, reaching ~0.45-0.50 after 180s with end slope ~0.0007-0.001/s still positive, staying below 0.6. A much smaller rise would indicate sub-linear gain or dead-zone; a much larger/faster rise would indicate super-linear gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input to hold y=0.5 and local gain around target; distinguishes u=0.5 holds band vs needs higher feedforward, which sets controller bias.
experiments.expected_observation: If u=0.5 steady state ~0.49 hypothesis is right, y starting ~0.502 will stay flat or decay very slightly to ~0.49-0.50 with end slope near 0 (+/-0.0003), remaining inside band 0.475-0.525. Continued rise would imply ss>0.51.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input to hold y=0.5 after E5 falsification; a step down to u=0.4 from above band discriminates whether ss(0.4) is near 0.5 versus still above, directly setting feedforward bias for control.
experiments.expected_observation: Starting ~0.534 under u=0.4, y will flatten then decay slowly toward band if ss(u=0.5)>0.534 hypothesis is right, reaching ~0.51-0.53 after 120s with small negative end slope and staying below 0.6. Continued rise would imply ss(u=0.4)>0.534 and even lower feedforward needed.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.5; distinguishes ss(0.45)~0.5 vs below/above, directly setting controller feedforward bias.
experiments.expected_observation: If u*=0.45 holds ~0.5 hypothesis is right, y starting ~0.491 will stay in band 0.475-0.525, flat or drifting slightly up to ~0.49-0.51 with end slope near zero (|slope|<0.0005). Continued decay below 0.48 would imply ss(0.45)<0.49; rise above 0.52 would imply ss(0.45)>0.52.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether u=0.45 truly holds y=0.5 over 240s total vs slow drift out of band; matters to set controller feedforward bias for 300s scoring.
experiments.expected_observation: If ss(0.45)~0.50 hypothesis is right, y starting ~0.497 stays in band 0.475-0.525 for full 120s, ending ~0.498-0.502 with end |slope|<0.0005. Steady rise above 0.51 would imply ss(0.45)>0.52; decay below 0.48 would imply ss(0.45)<0.48.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y with positive gain (heater warms sensor).
Response is first-order lag with tau ~140-160s; settling takes ~600s, so 100-180s holds do not fully settle unless starting near equilibrium and flat 5s slope can be quantization artifact.
There is no large dead zone: u=0.4-0.6 all produce clear response, including 0.05 steps around 0.45-0.5.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient near 0.05 due to heat loss to room.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear with gain ~1.0 and ambient ~0.05, i.e. ss(u)~0.05+1.0*u.
Steady-state input to hold y=0.5 is ~0.45 in (0.4,0.5): ss(0.5)>0.534 from E5 rise, ss(0.4)<0.491 from E6 decay, ss(0.45)~0.49-0.50 from E7 120s in-band hold.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) relative to control band width 0.05; quantization step ~0.005 with multi-sample plateaus causing zero 5s slope even while trending.
Initial response delay is short (<15s); rise/decay begins within ~6-20s of step, then slow exponential approach.
